description: Curated good threat scenarios (wording only) used as the reference vocabulary for the CM-17 threat-specificity check. Only name, attackActionDesc and weakness are read by the analyzer. Rebuilt by build_good_threats.py with a quality gate (min 8 words / 40 chars, no placeholder or reviewer-commentary text, deduplicated by wording).

ThreatScenarios.name: MC: Attack via Management Access
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc:
Adapt for Rancher-Management access: 
Attacker gets a user password, gets access and can then delete  the VMs. 
Permissions for deleting VM necessary: possible for certain users (username/PW, domain account in DE007) and
admin access (done via MyID MFA).
Or vulnerability in VSphere is exploited by an attacker, to get access to VSphere

ThreatScenarios.name: MC: Attack via Management Access --Manipulation
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc:
Same as  'Attack via Management Access'. 
Adapt for Rancher-Management access:
Attacker with user account comprises the VM, e.g. downloading the disk, manipulate it and upload it again.

ThreatScenarios.name: MC: Stealing password for the functional account (T-103 )
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: Attacker steals the credential (username/password) for the API ( Functional account).  Stored on SoCoSi server, used by the Pipeline Processing.

ThreatScenarios.name: MI: Malicious component (T-105)
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc:
Attacker uploads malicious component,  The component is unpacked, file names and metadata are parsed and saved. 
Then the scanners starts on the component.  With malicious content, the processing could crash.  Or the binary scanner could be affected. 
The attacker adds malicious text into the URL where to get the file from.  This could crash the Web server, or allow the attacker to take over the Web server.

ThreatScenarios.name: TA: Manipulated Docker Image (T-106)
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: A malicious image is downloaded from ??Docker Hub??.  The image is used as the basis for a container, which then contains malware.  The browser who looks up results on SoCoSi is affected.

ThreatScenarios.name: MI: Rogue container (T-107)
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: Attacker breaks out of other image by exploiting vulnerability in Container (VShere), and then gets acess on the Cluster level (Ubuntu Server).  With full access to the Cluster (Ubuntu server), anything could be done

ThreatScenarios.name: MI: Vulnerability of scanner exploited (T1)
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: Vulnerability in the scanner is exploited.  Would require the upload of  a malicious component that exploits the vulnerability. Could lead malicious code execution on the scanner.  Due to isolation, it is not possible to reach the outside.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Lack of patching for the binary scanner

ThreatScenarios.name: MI: Vulnerability in Scanner exploited to attack other containers (T-2)
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: Vulnerability in the scanner is exploited.  Would require the upload of  a malicious component that exploits the vulnerability. Could lead malicious code execution on the scanner.    A vulnerabiity in VSphere is exploited, and other images running on the VSpere instance are affected.

ThreatScenarios.name: TA: Manipulated Windows image (T-3)
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: ??Attacker in DE007 exploits vulnerability in SSH or Windows image on the binary scanner.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Up-to-date patch level might not be always possible for the binary scanner.

ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc:
Attacker misuses an account of a developer to get access to the folder and manipulates an app. 
The attacker needs to generate a ticket to trigger deployment, or needs to wait for the right point in time (developer updating the same app in the same branch).
Attacker gets access to folder in code.siemens.com by exploiting weaknesses in the implementation (not an authorized user)

Unauthorized access to app:
'Attacker gets access to an app (Liquitity gap analysis) and obtains report by getting access credentials of a legitimate user.
(Users cannot manipulate a report.)

ThreatScenarios.name: 4a
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc:
Malicous input via liquity gap anlysis or other apps:
Input does require 2-factor authentication and requires preconfigured account. So this attack is not relevant here.
Attacker (outsider) gets access to bastion host and from there to RStudio or Shiny server and steals private key for AWARD: SAP RFC technical user.

ThreatScenarios.name: 5a
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc:
Attacker (outsider in Internet or other AWS user) gets access to AWS subnet and from there to RStudio or Shiny server and steals credentials, manipulate apps etc. 

This threat was not rated because AWS configuration is considered to be secure, so likelihood is very low.

Attacker (insider with admin access)  accesses AWARD and gets data.
(SLA for admins cover access to bank data.)
Admin could add his GID to the PSE file if not already in there..
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Changes to the PSE file by admins are covered by tickets, but not logged. Techical user at AWARD, so at AWARD it is not possible to trace access to users.

ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc:
Attacker (insider with developer access) access AWARD and gets data. Only bank employees have access to bank data (Bankgeheimnis).

Developers have indidual accounts at AWARD, so this attack is not considered relevant.

ThreatScenarios.name: 7a
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: Attacker (outsider) gets access to bastion host and from there to RStudio or Shiny server and  manipulates apps or installs malicous code (own app or other apps) on Rstudio  in DEV via access from Bastion Host.

ThreatScenarios.name: 7b
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: Attacker (insider with developer access) manipulates apps or installs malicous code (own app or other apps) on Rstudio  in DEV via access from Bastion Host.

Unauthorized access to app:
Attacker gets access to Treasury app and changes data. Because of four eyes principle, the attacker needs access to two accounts (different GIDs)

Attacker (outsider) gets access to bastion host and from there to RStudio or Shiny server and steals password for MARS technical user and uses this to get access to MARS. MARS is located in the FiNavigate data center, and access is only possible for defined IP adresses  at the firewall.
Only IT has access to the directory where the password is stored for Prod.

Unauthorized access to app:
Attacker gets user access to MDH2.0.

Some app on the Shiny server uses all resources: This cannot affect MDH2.0 performance in the Kubernetes setting, as each app has its own container. 

Hence threat not relevant.

ThreatScenarios.name: Abuse stolen CI token to inject malicious release artifact
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker steals a CI/CD runner token, pushes a manipulated pipeline step, and publishes a signed-looking but malicious release artifact to the internal package repository.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Insufficient protection and rotation of CI/CD credentials, combined with weak pipeline integrity controls.

ThreatScenarios.name: Exploit missing certificate validation on OPC UA client connection
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker performs a machine-in-the-middle attack on OPC UA traffic by presenting an untrusted server certificate to a client that does not enforce certificate pinning or trust validation.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Improper OPC UA certificate trust validation and missing endpoint authentication hardening.

ThreatScenarios.name: Upload forged firmware image through insecure update workflow
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker uploads a forged firmware package to the update service and triggers installation on field devices because signature verification is incomplete or can be bypassed in maintenance mode.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Insecure firmware verification workflow and weak authorization around maintenance update paths.

ThreatScenarios.name: Perform credential stuffing on exposed engineering web portal
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker uses leaked corporate credentials and automated login attempts against an exposed engineering portal to gain operator access and modify runtime parameters.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Missing rate limiting and weak account lockout or multi-factor authentication on internet-reachable login endpoints.

ThreatScenarios.name: Inject unauthorized MQTT control messages into OT broker
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker connects to an MQTT broker without strong client authentication and publishes forged control topics that trigger unsafe state changes in downstream controllers.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Insufficient MQTT topic authorization and missing mutual authentication for broker clients.

ThreatScenarios.name: Exfiltrate historian backups from misconfigured object storage
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker enumerates publicly exposed object storage buckets and downloads historical process backups containing sensitive production data and configuration snapshots.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Misconfigured cloud storage access policies and missing encryption or access monitoring for backup archives.

ThreatScenarios.name: Exploit unsafe deserialization in telemetry ingestion API
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker submits crafted payloads to the telemetry ingestion API to trigger unsafe deserialization, resulting in remote code execution in the processing service.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Use of insecure deserialization libraries and missing strict schema validation on inbound API payloads.

ThreatScenarios.name: Pivot from vendor remote access jump host into OT segment
ThreatScenarios.attackActionDesc: An attacker compromises a vendor remote access jump host and laterally moves into the OT segment because network segmentation and session controls are insufficiently enforced.
ThreatScenarios.weakness: Overly permissive trust relationships between remote maintenance infrastructure and OT network zones.
